name: Pohlman, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Condemarin's limited holding does not apply to the 2017 GIA's damages cap because the statutes are different and Condemarin lacked a majority rationale.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Concurred, argued that the court clarified the Brickey standard regarding prosecutorial refiling of charges, vacated the lower court's dismissal, and remanded the case for re-evaluation under the new standard.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE DURRANT
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, holding that the PWS's procedural rules violate separation of powers.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Recused himself and did not participate.

name: JUSTICE HAGEN
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion affirming the district court's injunction because the ballot title was misleading and the constitutional publication requirements were not met.

name: DURRANT, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Baugh's counsel was ineffective for failing to request specific unanimity instructions, creating an unacceptable risk of a non-unanimous verdict.

name: DURRANT, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the property tax exemption applies only when a nonprofit entity uses its property exclusively for charitable purposes, and Sports Medicine did not meet this standard because its market-rate testing and vacant space were not exclusively charitable uses.

name: JUSTICE POHLMAN
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, affirming that the statute of repose is constitutional as Bingham failed to show it violated the Open Courts Clause, Uniform Operation of Laws Provision, or Equal Protection Clause.

name: Justice Hagen
description: Concurred, arguing that the County failed to demonstrate the Aircraft Valuation Law was unconstitutional as applied or on its face.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, arguing that Kell's five-year delay in filing his petition, after discovering new evidence, was not excused by ineffective assistance of prior counsel and did not violate his constitutional rights under the PCRA's time and procedural bars.

name: Justice Lee
description: Did not participate in the consideration of the case.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Did not participate in the consideration of the case.

name: Associate Chief Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution's Bail Provision does not forbid judges from setting bail for defendants not guaranteed bail, but rather allows judicial discretion.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, argued that improper jury contacts by authoritative figures trigger a rebuttable presumption of prejudice, requiring the State to prove harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt.

name: Justice Petersen
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's balancing test for prejudice is novel and distorts existing precedent, and that the district court's handling of the matter already satisfied the standard.

name: Lee
description: Concurred, authored the opinion affirming the dismissal of zoning challenges and retaining jurisdiction for tax provisions.

name: Himonas
description: Did not rule as he retired before the court's opinion was finalized.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Authored the majority opinion, concluding Laws lacked standing to challenge Grayeyes's election and affirming the denial of attorney fees to Grayeyes.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Laws lacked standing due to not identifying a private injury and that Grayeyes was not entitled to attorney fees under the private attorney general doctrine.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution's standing requirements should be re-examined, questioning the reliance on federal precedents and inconsistencies in state jurisprudence.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the PCRA time-bars most of Patterson's claims, the courts have constitutional writ authority independent of the PCRA, but Patterson failed to show the time-bars violate his constitutional rights.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred in the judgment and central elements of the majority opinion, but objected to other elements as unnecessary and unsupported, particularly the majority's analysis of the legislature's substantive regulatory power over writs.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, argued that individuals have a common-law right to change their legal sex designation and courts have authority to adjudicate such petitions.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred in judgment, but argued the legislature intended a 'proper cause' standard for sex changes, treating it similarly to name changes, and objective evidence is one way to show proper cause.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Dissented, argued the court lacked jurisdiction for non-adversarial matters and that the statute refers to biological sex, not gender identity, without delegating policymaking power to courts.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, arguing that while the Limitations on Landowner Liability Act can bar wrongful death claims and is constitutional, the plaintiffs sufficiently alleged that the death was not caused by an inherent risk, thus reversing the dismissal and remanding the case.
